title: Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and More Who Were in the Running as Next James Bond
text:
James Bond: Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, More Up for Robert Pattinson Role 
 News Photos Videos Shopping Black Friday Kardashians Couples Influencers Red Carpet Royals TV Scoop News Photos Videos Shopping Black Friday Kardashians Couples Influencers Red Carpet Royals TV Scoop Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and More Who Were in the Running as Next James Bond
 Robert Pattinson was officially announced as the next James Bond, succeeding Daniel Craig to play the iconic secret agent. See Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and more stars who circulated the role. 
 By Olivia Evans Nov 16, 2026 6:04 PM | Updated 7 hours ago Tags Movies James Bond Celebrities Nicholas Hoult Link Copied Add E! News to Google Watch : Next James Bond Revealed After Years-Long Search: See His First Teaser Looking for someone? The name’s Pattinson,  Robert Pattinson . 
 But before the  Primetime  actor was officially announced as the next James Bond, succeeding  Daniel Craig  in playing the iconic secret agent, there were plenty of other could-be stars vying to star in  Denis Villeneuve ’s next movie.
 Following months of speculation about the next 007, a rumored short list began circulating in October, with multiple outlets citing Jack Lowden ,  Josh O’Connor, Jacob Elordi  and  Callum Turner  among the contenders. While the actors went method when it came to keeping their potential casting as the secret agent under wraps, they were, at least, willing to react to the rumors. 
 For his part, O’Connor admitted it was “extraordinary” to even be considered. 
 “It’s an incredibly bizarre pinch me moment,”  The Crown  alum told the BBC in October , “even being uttered in that same sentence and being considered for something like that.”
 Similarly, Lowden had  Slow Horses  costar had Gary Oldman  expressing he should be the next Bond, and that itself was an honor.
 read Next James Bond Revealed After Years-Long Search: See His First Teaser “It’s nice to be mentioned—for any role—and I’m just not really going to add to the noise,” Lowden told British GQ  in an interview published earlier this month. “It’s very nice, and Gary’s a sweetheart. It’s particularly lovely, coming from someone like him. But I don’t really listen to it.”
 As for Turner, he held firm that he had no information about the role in a June interview, although he did divulge that his casting was a question he couldn’t get away from—even in his most personal circles. 
 “I'll tell you what's so funny about the Bond thing: Even your best friends ask you, people text you that you haven't spoken to for 10 years—and you know nothing!” he told  The Hollywood Reporter   at the time. “It's such a weird thing of something happening and nothing happening at all. I genuinely know nothing. I just find it quite amusing.”
 Brendon Thorne/Daniele Venturelli/WireImage/Amy Sussman/Getty Images In addition to Pattinson,  Nicholas Hoult  was also recently added to the shortlist for the iconic character, but his  How to Rob a Bank  costar  Pete Davidson  gave a cheeky assist when it came to sharing any details on his audition process.  
 “It’s going to be me,” Davidson told E! News in an interview alongside Hoult earlier this month . “I will be the first American James Bond.”
 Still, when it came to the possibility of Hoult getting cast, Davidson emphasized that, in his opinion, Hoult was “the best guy for the job.”
 Meanwhile, Elordi and  Aaron Taylor-Johnson  also shared their perspective on the speculations that they too could be the seventh actor to officially portray the  Ian Fleming character. Elordi dodged the speculation when he chalked his August visit to London to a simple weekend away—as opposed to a potential Bond audition— telling Variety , “I’m here on holiday.”
 For Taylor-Johnson’s part, he reacted to rumors that he would take over the part from Craig—whose fifth and final outing as Bond was  No Time to Die  in 2021—by emphasizing that he was happy enough to see where life takes him. 
 “I don’t feel like I need to have a future drawn out for me,” Taylor-Johnson told  Rolling Stone UK  in 2024 . “I feel like: whatever’s drawn out for me, I can f--kin’ do better.”
 For more iconic roles that nearly went to other stars, keep reading… 
 Presley Ann Photo/for Sundance; Virginia Sherwood/Nbc-Tv/Kobal Glen Powell as Tim Riggins on  Friday Night Lights 
 The Top Gun: Maverick star tried out for multiple parts on  Friday Night Lights , including the main role that Taylor Kitsch played.
 Jon Kopaloff/FilmMagic / SGranitz/WireImage Chris Pine as Ryan Atwood on The O.C. 
 The Star Trek actor lost out on the role, which ultimately went to Ben McKenzie , due to his bad acne.
 "I had awful skin as a teenager," he said on Josh Horowitz 's podcast Happy Sad Confused in May 2024, "and then I when I came after college, my skin started breaking out again."
 Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images/Ron P. Jaffe/CBS Jason Biggs as Ted Mosby on How I Met Your Mother 
 "I was offered the role and it's probably my biggest regret, you know, on passing," the  American Pie alum revealed in a 2021 SiriusXM interview. "I think I was in a phase of, at the time—it sounds so obnoxious to say right now—but at the time it was like, 'OK, do I want to do TV?' I don't know that I was quite ready to go that route."
 Randy Holmes/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images; Todd Williamson/Getty Images Rob Lowe as Derek Shepherd on Grey's Anatomy 
 The Parks and Recreation alum revealed that he turned down the role of McDreamy in his 2014 memoir, and it came back up in an episode of Marc Maron 's podcast.
 "That's probably cost me $70 million," Lowe joked. "Eh, it's just money."
 The actor added that he did watch the pilot when it came out and "when they started calling the handsome doctor 'McDreamy,' I was like, 'yeah, that's not for me.'" 
 Roy Rochlin/Getty Images, Moviestore/Shutterstock Benedict Cumberbatch as Bill Compton on True Blood 
 The Sherlock star auditioned for the role of vampire Bill Compton back in the day. Stephen Moyer went on to land the part.
 Gary Gershoff/WireImage, Moviestore/Shutterstock Jessica Chastain as Sookie Stackhouse on True Blood 
 Before she was an Oscar winner, the Eyes of Tammy Faye actress read for the role of Sookie Stackhouse. The part eventually went to Anna Paquin .
 VALERIE MACON/AFP/Getty Images, Jeffrey Mayer/WireImage Jennifer Lawrence as Crystal Norris on True Blood 
 The Hunger Games star read for the part of werepanther—and almost got the part—but her young age at the time played a factor in the part going to another actress. Lindsay Pulsipher landed the gig.
 Axelle/Bauer-Griffin/FilmMagic, Warner Bros. Television Tiffani Thiessen as Rachel Green on Friends 
 The Saved By the Bell veteran said she auditioned for the iconic role, but she was ultimately too young for the part.
 Monica Schipper/Getty Images, Cbs Television/Entertainment Pictures via ZUMA Press) Katherine Langford as Betty Cooper on Riverdale 
 Riverdale 's Camila Mendes said the 13 Reasons Why star was one of the actresses who auditioned for the role of the iconic blonde. As she told Entertainment Weekly , "I remember we went out and we got falafel with a guy who was auditioning for Archie."
 Getty Images Katherine Heigl as Jen Lindley on Dawson's Creek 
 It's hard to imagine anyone else playing Capeside's resident NYC transplant, but as creator Kevin Williamson revealed to Entertainment Weekly , the role of almost went to the Grey's Anatomy star.
  "She looked slightly older at that time. Even though she was younger, I just think she was more mature," Williamson recalled. "She gave a great audition, I remember we were all sort of like, ‘Wow, she's good.'"
 However, the part ultimately went to Michelle Williams .
 Getty Images Selma Blair as Joey Potter on Dawson's Creek 
 According to Williamson, the role of Dawson Leery's lovesick BFF was actually the Cruel Intention actress' to lost.
 "I really loved Selma until, of course, I got the infamous videotape from the basement of the Holmes family in Toledo, Ohio," he said of Katie Holmes ' last-minute auditon. "And when that video showed up, it changed my whole life."
 Getty Images Lisa Edelstein as Carrie Bradshaw in Sex and the City 
 The House star was so close to taking on the iconic role of Carrie Bradshaw that she even had a completed contract. In the end, however, she was just the back-up to the producers' first choice, Sarah Jessica Parker .
 "I was either going to do it or not. It all depended on whether she said yes," Edelstein said. "My contract was complete. I was waiting."
 Ashley Olsen as Serena van der Woodsen on Gossip Girl 
 Initially, The CW wanted the Full House alum as our favorite beautiful blonde Upper East Sider, but casting director David Rapaport only had eyes for Lively.
 "I was terrified we wouldn't get her or they wouldn't like her," he told BuzzFeed , "because, honestly, the show lived and died on her and I had absolutely no other ideas."
 Rumer Willis as Blair Waldorf on Gossip Girl 
 The CW wanted Bruce Willis and Demi Moore 's oldest daughter as the Gossip Girl lead, but casting director Rapaport knew she wasn't right for the role (and would eventually cast her on 90210 ).
 "I love Rumer," he told BuzzFeed. "She's grown into quite an amazing actress and person, but that, to me, was based on protecting the investment of a television show where creatively, these lesser-known girls really captured the essence of the show and carried it for six years."
 Ken Ishii/Getty Images/James Devaney/WireImage Alden Ehrenreich as Dan Humphrey on Gossip Girl 
 Rapaport told Entertainment Weekly that he "desperately" wanted the Star Wars: A Solo Story actor to be Lonely Boy, but producers thought he was too short to play Blake Lively 's love interest.
 Getty Images; Kharen Hill/The CW Keke Palmer as Iris West on The Flash 
 Produces said nope to the Disney Channel alum because they felt she was "felt a little too young" next to Grant Gustin , who played the titular superhero, according to Rapaport.
 The role ventually went to Candice Patton .
 "We had seen Candice initially," he remembered, "but I think we were too early on in the process to cast her so we ended up testing Keke Palmer and this other girl."
 Helen Sloan/courtesy of HBO Iwan Rheon as Jon Snow on Game of Thrones 
 Before the Battle of the Bastards, there was a battle between Rheon and Kit Harington for to actual role of Jon Snow.
 "I auditioned for the pilot of Game of Thrones , and was down to the last two for Jon Snow," he told The Telegraph , saying that everything eventually worked out when he landed the role of season five villain Ramsay Snow. 
 "Ramsay is the complete polar opposite," he added. "In my mind, I secretly thought it was Ramsay."
 NBC, Getty Images Chris Pratt as Chuck on Chuck 
 After working with the Guardians of the Galaxy star on the final season of The O.C. , Josh Schwartz revealed Pratt was his first choice for the role that eventually went to Zachary Levi. 
 "He was the first guy I wanted to play 'Chuck'. But as fate would have it, he was destined to guard the galaxy, not the Buy More," Schwartz revealed. "And might I add, couldn't happen to a nicer guy."
 Ilya S. Savenok/Getty Images, Jessica Miglio/Netflix Katie Holmes as Piper on Orange Is the New Black 
 The Dawson's Creek veteran met with Orange Is the New Black creator Jenji Kohan early in the show's development, Kohan revealed . Holmes, who is an admitted fan of the series, had "other things to do," Kohan told E! News. "And also in the beginning no one knew what this was."
 Cobie Smulders as Kate on Lost 
 Yep, Robin Scherbatsky could have been Kate Austen, and two of our favorite shows were almost very different, according to Cobie Smulders .
 Both she and Evangeline Lilly   were "testing for  Lost ," Smulders revealed to E! News in 2014 . "She owes a lot to me because I went in and I bombed the audition. And she was like, 'Thank you!'"
 Helen Hunt, Ashley Judd as Alicia on The Good Wife 
 Everybody knows The Good Wife is Julianna Margulies ' show, but that almost wasn't the case. The Emmy winner revealed the studio wanted Ashley Judd and Helen Hunt  before she got the gig.
 Christopher Polk/Getty Images; WB Katie Holmes as Buffy on Buffy the Vampire Slayer 
 Hard to imagine anyone else hunting down vampires in Sunnydale, but the Dawson's Creek actress almost had the title role in the WB series. Holmes turned it down to go to high school, and Sarah Michelle Gellar was cast.
 Charles Sykes/Bravo/NBCU Photo Bank via Getty Images; HBO Lorraine Bracco as Carmela Soprano on The Sopranos 
 Before taking her place in the chair as psychiatrist Jennifer Melfi, the Oscar nominee turned down playing mobster wife Carmela Soprano because she had portrayed a similar part in Goodfellas . The role eventually went to Edie Falco .
 Frazer Harrison/Getty Images; Mitch Haaseth/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images Taraji P. Henson as Olivia Pope on Scandal 
 Before she was breaking records on Fox's Empire , the Oscar nominee  revealed she had auditioned to be Scandal 's ultimate fixer, Olivia Pope. "When I went in to read for Shonda Rhimes , in my mind I was like, 'This is Kerry Washington . Why am I even in here?'" she said. "It was hers."
 Ian Gavan/Getty Images; Jaap Buitendijk/Focus/Kobal/Shutterstock Gillian Anderson as Lady Cora on Downton Abbey 
 Can you imagine Agent Scully residing in Downton Abbey? It almost happened, but the X Files star turned down the role that eventually went to Elizabeth McGovern .
 Henry S. Dziekan III/Getty Images; CW Network/Kobal/Shutterstock Ashlee Simpson as Elena on The Vampire Diaries 
 It's hard to imagine anyone else playing Elena Gilbert on the CW hit series, but the "Pieces of Me" singer was the network's first choice. It wasn't until the producers took a second look at Nina Dobrev 's audition tape that they decided to go with the Bulgarian beauty.
 Ron Galella/WireImage; NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images Whitney Houston as Sondra on The Cosby Show 
 The legendary singer was offered the lead role in Bill Cosby -led series, but passed to pursue her music career. The oldest Huxtable daughter was ultimately portrayed by Sabrina Le Beauf .
 ABC; HBO Dana Delany as Carrie on Sex and the City 
 To Sex and the City fans, Sarah Jessica Parker is Carrie Bradshaw, but once upon a time, Delany was offered the role of the New York columnist. The Emmy-winner passed because she had already done multiple projects involving x-rated material ( Nude Girls , Exit to Eden ) and didn't want to be involved with a project that had "sex" in the title.
 NBC; Jim Spellman/WireImage Paul Schaffer as George on Seinfeld 
 David Letterman 's former late night show bandleader was offered the role by Jerry Seinfeld without an audition, but Shaffer never called him back. Jason Alexander  was cast after submitting an audition tape featuring a Woody Allen impression.
 Charley Gallay/Getty Images; Jaimie Trueblood/AMC Thomas Jane as Don on Mad Men 
 AMC wanted the Boogie Nights actor, but Jon Hamm said during a podcast that Jane passed because he didn't want to be on a television show. Of course, Jane would go on to star in HBO's Hung .
